title: Infostealers Are Stealing Cloud and AI Credentials From Infected Devices
content_md: An infostealer infection on a developer’s laptop or personal computer can become an entry point into an organization’s cloud, source code, and AI services. The malware searches the device for passwords, API keys, and login tokens, then sends them to attackers who can use them to access business systems. In research published September 25, Wiz analyzed secrets detected on infected machines through its integration with NordStellar. Lumma C2, RedLine, and Vidar accounted for 85.7% of the detected incidents. Among the compromised secrets, 46% were associated with AWS, 13% with Google Cloud, roughly 10% with GitHub, and 5% with AI platforms , mainly OpenAI API keys. These figures describe Wiz’s analyzed data, not all infostealer infections. Infostealers Steal Cloud AI Credentials Infostealers often reach users through phishing, fake software downloads, or malicious advertising. A separate route targets developers through compromised software packages. Once running, the malware can collect saved browser data and files holding credentials. Operators package the stolen information into logs, which may be sold to brokers or used directly to break into organizations. A stolen session cookie is especially dangerous. It represents a login the user has already completed. If an attacker can reuse a valid cookie, they may enter the service without facing a new multifactor authentication prompt .
